I am 53 years old and have farmed my whole life in Quzhou County. I have 8 mu of good flat land, and I know this soil well. Every year I grow winter wheat and then summer maize on the same fields — this is what my family has always done, and it is the most reliable way to feed ourselves and earn some cash. I do not grow cotton anymore because my husband and I are getting older, and cotton needs too many pesticide sprays and too much bending down. I also do not try new crops like stevia because I only went to primary school and I do not trust myself to manage something I do not understand. For wheat, I buy improved seeds from the shop — this year probably luyuan502 or something similar — and I rotary till before sowing in October. I put down compound fertilizer as basal and topdress with urea in the spring when the wheat turns green. I irrigate four times: once in winter to protect from frost, and then at green-up, jointing, and grain filling if the rain is not enough. For maize, I plant hybrid seeds like denghai605 right after the wheat harvest in early June. I do not till for maize — I sow directly into the wheat stubble to save time and diesel. I apply compound fertilizer once at sowing, and I irrigate twice if it is dry. For both crops I spray pesticides three or four times, mainly for weeds and corn borers. I expect about 550 kg per mu from the wheat and about 550 kg per mu from the maize. This plan is safe, it uses what I know, and it keeps my family fed.
